title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 by US marshals while babysitting four children. She was falsely charged in North Dakota with four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft. She spent about six months in jail, nearly four months without bail awaiting extradition and about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee when the Fargo fraud happened. She was released on Christmas Eve.

Lipps is suing for $10m in federal court against the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck. She says police wrongly relied on AI facial recognition, which matched her social media photo to a fake ID used by a suspect. She says she did not look like the suspect and had never been to North Dakota. The lawsuit claims the police department lacked proper policy, training, and supervision for facial recognition. A Fargo spokesperson said the city does not comment on pending litigation.
